{"id":640764,"title":"(ENR SUCC) DEV & TEST - 834E/U AR PASSE Transaction Effective Date Logic Update - EDI","description":"<p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><strong></strong> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;font-weight:400;\"> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><strong>Overview</strong> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">This feature details the functionality required to correct the improper entry of split spans in Facets, based on Eligibility Date and Assessment Date, for changes received via EDI 834 E and U. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Business Rules &amp; Requirements </h3><ol style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date 2000 Loop (DTP*356/DTP*348) from the EDI 834 as the transaction effective date for all new enrollments, regardless of the Assessment Date. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date = 1/24/25, use Eligibility Date (1/31/25). </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility, if the Assessment Date has changed. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date changes to 6/29/25, use Assessment Date (6/29/25). </li><li>The business needs to update the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility when the Assessment Date changes, but none of the other elements listed below have changed:<ul><li>Assessment Number </li><li>Assessment Tier </li><li>Assessment Division </li><li>Aid Category </li><li>Rate Cell </li><li>Pregnancy </li> </ul> </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received prior to the Eligibility Date. </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Maintenance Date (DTP*303) as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received after the Eligibility Date. </li> </ol><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Current State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">Currently, Maintenance effective date is being used to split spans on Update files. This is causing mismatches with capitation calculations, and the Finance team is misreporting revenue. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">What is Changing </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date 2000 Loop (DTP*303) cannot be used for all change transactions. Depending on the change, and whether it is received prior to or after the initial Eligibility Date, the transaction effective date may reflect either the Assessment Date, Eligibility Date, or Maintenance Date. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Future State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date will no longer be used to split spans based on Update (834) files, except as detailed in Requirement 4 above. The transaction dates in Facets will conform to the functionality detailed in Requirements 1-5. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Assumptions </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">None identified. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Dependencies/Considerations </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">None identified. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Risks </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New # Agent 2 — Test Scenario Generation (User Story → Test Scenarios)




## ROLE




You are a test scenario generation agent for EDI 834 inbound files. You receive user story details from the previous agent (Agent 1) and generate only test scenarios (not test cases) derived strictly from the combination of the description and acceptance criteria of that user story.




## INPUT




- User story details are passed in from the previous agent (Agent 1). Do NOT call Azure DevOps directly. Use the user story content, description, and acceptance criteria provided to you by Agent 1.




- This includes, word for word and without summarization:




  - The full Description — every line, every bullet, every section




  - The full Acceptance Criteria — every AC scenario, every Given/When/Then line, the full Definition of Ready (DoR), and the full Definition of Done (DoD)




## INSTRUCTIONS




1. Consume the user story details received from the previous agent (Agent 1), including title, description, acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then), Definition of Ready, and Definition of Done for EDI 834 inbound files.




2. Parse and semantically analyze both the description and the acceptance criteria together — including every Given/When/Then line, DoR, and DoD — to extract functional and non-functional requirements. Generate test scenarios that are very specific to the description and acceptance criteria combined, as provided by Agent 1 [MUST]. The description often carries contextual/business intent that must be used alongside the acceptance criteria to shape each scenario — acceptance criteria alone MUST NOT be treated as the sole source.




3. Treat DoR as the precondition/setup context (what must be true before the scenario can be executed) and DoD as the completion/exit criteria (what confirms the scenario is fully satisfied). Use both to shape preconditions and expected outcomes at the scenario level — do NOT ignore or drop DoR/DoD content when generating scenarios [MUST].




4. Reference the provided EDI 834 knowledge base and historical manual test scenarios to understand how the scenarios should be framed and all the different situations that need to be covered. Generate test scenarios that are specific to EDI 834 inbound and refer the process steps in the knowledge base STRICTLY [MUST].




5. Generate comprehensive and specific test scenarios covering positive, negative, and edge conditions, ensuring all possible situations are included, and generate them based on the description and acceptance criteria combination (including Given/When/Then, DoR, DoD) specific to inbound [MUST].




6. Produce only test scenarios — a concise, one-line statement of what is to be validated for each acceptance criterion, informed by the corresponding description context. Do NOT generate detailed test steps, expected results, or full test cases (that is Agent 3's responsibility).




7. For each test scenario, populate the fields: `scenarioId`, `title`, `descriptionRef`, `acceptanceCriteriaRef` (Given/When/Then text), `dorRef`, `dodRef`, `type` (Positive / Negative / Edge), `description`, and `priority`.




8. Validate each scenario against formatting and content rules; if any validation fails, regenerate the scenario until full compliance is achieved.




9. Provide error handling for missing data, incomplete stories, or knowledge base gaps with fallback strategies (e.g., flag the gap in the scenario `description` and continue with the remaining criteria). If the description, DoR, or DoD is missing or empty, fall back to acceptance-criteria-only generation and flag this in the `description` field.




STRICT RULES:




- NEVER replace the description, acceptance criteria, Given/When/Then lines, DoR, or DoD with a summary line.




- NEVER paraphrase, consolidate, shorten, or omit any part of them.




- Do NOT hallucinate — every scenario must be traceable to the description, AC (Given/When/Then), DoR, DoD, or KB provided.




## SCENARIO VOLUME DISCIPLINE [MUST]




- Produce a MAXIMUM of 4 test scenarios per user story. This is a hard limit.




- When the user story contains more than 4 candidate scenarios, select the 4 that carry the highest business risk and the widest coverage of the acceptance criteria, and set `priority` accordingly (High first). Merge closely related acceptance criteria into a single scenario rather than dropping coverage silently.




- Every scenario you emit MUST be materially different from the others. Do NOT emit near-duplicate scenarios that validate the same mechanism with different wording.




- This limit exists because the downstream test case generator expands every scenario into 3 test cases of 15-20 steps each, and the platform enforces a 600-second execution ceiling on the workflow. Exceeding 4 scenarios causes the downstream run to time out and produce nothing.




## OUTPUT FORMAT




- JSON array of test scenario objects. Each object must contain:




  - `scenarioId` — unique identifier (e.g., `TS_001`)




  - `title` — short scenario name




  - `descriptionRef` — the relevant excerpt from the user story description that informs this scenario




  - `acceptanceCriteriaRef` — the acceptance criterion (full Given/When/Then text) this scenario maps to




  - `dorRef` — the relevant Definition of Ready item(s), if any, that this scenario depends on. Use an empty string if the user story has no Definition of Ready — do NOT invent one.




  - `dodRef` — the relevant Definition of Done item(s), if any, that confirm this scenario's completion. Use an empty string if the user story has no Definition of Done — do NOT invent one.




  - `type` — `Positive` | `Negative` | `Edge`




  - `description` — one-line statement of what is validated, reflecting the description, AC, DoR, and DoD context




  - `priority` — `High` | `Medium` | `Low`




- Data must be clean, validated, and ready to be consumed by the next agent (Agent 3).




- Emit the JSON array and nothing else. No prose before or after it.




## SAMPLE

3.10.2. Other Member Details Lookup
The requirements for Address Type Lookup are as follows: -
· If Loop 2000/2100D/NM1 Segment (Member Employer) is present then ENR should set the Member Type value in the ECF as “1”.
· If Loop 2000/2100E/NM1 Segment (Member School) is present then ENR should set the Member Type value in the ECF as “2”.
· If Loop 2000/2100F/NM1 Segment (Custodial Parent) is present then ENR should set the Member Type value in the ECF as “3”.
· If Loop 2000/2100G/NM1 Segment (Responsible Person) is present then ENR should set the Member Type value in the ECF as “4”.
· If Loop 2000/2100H/NM1 Segment (Drop Off Location) is present then ENR should set the Member Type value in the ECF as “5”.
· ENR should be configured to read these codes from a configuration File.

	Priority
	This will not come in the file but we need to use it once we are done with filtering based on all other criteria. 
	 



3.10.4.3. Steps to derive AidCat using crosswalk table
1. Identify all the records from the crosswalk with matching derived GRGR_ID.
2. Identify all the record from the crosswalk with matching ‘AssistanceGroupCode’ as well as those records having AssistanceGroupCode as ‘NULL’.
3. Identify all the record from the crosswalk with matching derived ‘Program’ as well as those records having Program as ‘NULL’.
4. Identify all the record from the crosswalk with matching ‘Capitation_Rate_Ind_Pattern’ as well as those records having Capitation_Rate_Ind_Pattern as ‘NULL’.
5. Identify all the record from the crosswalk with matching ‘LTC_Ind’ based on value of HD04 from 2300 loop as well as those records having LTC_Ind as ‘NULL’.
If there is any loop with HD04 = NH-MCP then the outcome will be “Y”.
6. Identify all the record from the crosswalk with matching ‘SNF_Ind’ based on value of HD04 from 2300 loop as well as those records having SNF_Ind as ‘NULL’.
If there is any loop with HD04 = WVR-ICDS then the outcome will be “Y”.

1. Introduction
The purpose of this Fit Gap and scope document is to provide clarity to both CareSource and Edifecs teams on various business requirements for implementation of Edifecs Enrollment Management (“ENR”) solution. This includes but is not limited to: Mapping of CareSource’s requirements to Edifecs Enrollment Management solution’s features and functions, classification of requirements into categories identifying different degrees of feature match and also overview the implementation assumptions. This document will cover implementation of the Edifecs ENR Solution & Approach.
The document provides high level information about how the out of box Edifecs Enrollment Management solution can be implemented along with comparisons to Edifecs product based on particular requirements. It shall also provide insight in with regards to how CareSource would like the solution to be configured to meet business requirements. The Technical details of this implementation are out of scope for this document and instead shall be covered by a separate Technical Design document.
1.1. Definitions
The below terms have been used to define certain aspects of the Edifecs solution and the work effort involved for the relative requirement:
· Out of box – This term clarifies that the requirement associated with this work effort is a pre-defined functionality which is implemented as part of the ENR Product 8.11 and does not require any customization.
· Configuration – This term is used to specify that the associated requirement is not out of the box and will involve some effort on the implementation consultants’ part to configure.
· Customization –This term has been used to denote that the associated requirement is a complex code and will take significant effort (custom code) to implement.

· Not Supported – With current product offering and in given timelines, the requested requirement cannot be supported by customization or Custom development.

2. Solution Overview

1.1. Business Problem and Solution
CareSource currently utilizes multiple homegrown systems and solutions together to process Ohio State Medicaid enrollment files. CareSource EDI Team picks up the x12 834 files and push these to preprocessor where business validations are performed. Once the records are identified as good then it is splits into ~14 flat files. Facets is updated via batch process using MMS keyword file processing. There also exists a custom-built reconciliation tool that compares intake enrollment data against data posted to Facets at end of the day and provides list of errors to enrollment recon specialists to work through.
Edifecs ENR will bring in industry standard EDI compliance validation and acknowledgement generation best practices. Edifecs ENR will also bring file sequencing, tracking, alerting mechanisms as well as intuitive user interface for EDI data management. Edifecs ENR provides drools-based rules framework that will be utilized to implement large amount of current Facets validations in Edifecs layer. These validations put erroneous transactions into Edifecs ENR workflow for manual review and intervention, thus ensuring only cleaned and validated enrollment data goes downstream to existing enrollment services layer.

3.16. Member Matching Logic
The business rules for Member Matching Logic are as follows. 

3.16.1. Medicaid ID
· SearchMember based on the MEDICAID ID (Loop 2000->REF*0F). The output of SearchMember would provide the MEME_CK within the same group.
· If the MEME_CK is found, then the member is present based on the Medicaid ID.
3.16.2. Prior Medicaid Id 
If the member is not found using the Medicaid Id, then check to see if the member exists in the MEST using he prior Medicaid ID (REF*Q4)
3.16.3. Date of Birth, SSN and Name
· ENR should check if the member is present in Facets based on DOB, SSN, First Name and Last Name using the FXI API. If MEME_CK is found, then the member is present in Facets.
· If the SSN is not 9-digit valid numeric value (for e.g. 9999999999, 000000000) then do no use the SSN for match by demographics. Just use first name, last name and DOB. 
· If there are multiple MEME_CK found, then ENR should error out the transa

[Source: direct_files, File: CareSource_EdifecsENR_FitGapAnalysis_MIv1.2.docx, Chunk: 14/null]
Need to check if 2100B loop is received and there is no 2100A present in change transactions.	Comment by Surendra Dangi: Based on prod file review with Ryan and Rameeza state is not sending 2100B loop instead 2100A loop is coming with NM101 as 74 with INS03=001 & INS04=25.
· Verify is SSN length is not 9 Characters
· Verify is SSN 000000000
ENR will check if the SSN is present in the inbound File.
If yes, then ENR will check if the SSN Length is not equal to 9 characters or SSN value is “000000000”.
If yes and the ErrorType = “Partial”, then ENR will check if the Member is present in Facets. If yes, then ENR would retrieve the SSN value from Facets. If SSN is present in Facets then ENR will update the inbound SSN value with Facets Value and log an event “Invalid SSN and it has been updated with Facets value”. If SSN is not present in Facets then ENR will log an event “Invalid Inbound SSN and Facets SSN is not present. Inbound SSN is blank” and it would blank the Inbound SSN. If member is not present in FACETS, then ENR would log an event “New Member so updating the inbound SSN with NULL value” and it would blank the inbound SSN.
If yes and the ErrorType = “FATAL”, then ENR would move the transaction into Exception and log an error “Invalid SSN”.
If yes and the ErrorType = “WARNING”, then ENR would log an event “Invalid SSN”.
This rule is applicable for daily Changes Only and Audit Files (Add/Change/Term/Reinstate transaction).

Default Severity – Partial for all.

3.6.30. TermDateMissing	
The requirements for this validation are as follows:
This validation looks at the raw 834 data at the following Element 2000: 2300: DTP349 and verifies the following scenario: -
· If the termination Date is 1/1/1753 or 9999/12/31 for all transactions other than TERM.
· If it is a term transaction and the termination Date is missing.
If the ErrorType is set as Fatal then ENR should log a with the following message “Eligibility Termination Date is not present or invalid” and the transaction should be moved into Exception WorkList.
If the ErrorType is set as Partial then ENR should log an event with the following message “Eligibility Termination Date is not present or invalid”.
If the ErrorType is set as Warning then ENR should log an event with the following message “Eligibility Termination Date is not present or invalid”.
This rule is applicable for daily Changes Only (Term transaction) Files.

Default Severity – Term: Fatal.

3.6.31. TermDtFacetsTermDtMismatch		Comment by Surendra Dangi: Not needed for MI.
The requirements for this validation are as follows:
This validation looks at the raw 834 data at the following Element 2000: 2300:DTP349 and verifies the following scenario: -
· Verifies if the TERM DATE in the Raw 834 File is greater than the Termination Date in Facets. 
ENR will check if the Member is present in Facets. If yes, then ENR will extract the Eligibility Effective and Eligbility Term Date from the intake file (first instance of DTP*348).
ENR will check if the GroupID CSIN is configured for the following validation “TermDtFacetsTermDtMismatchUseSGSGID” in the configuration table 
If yes, ENR will extract the TERM DATE from Facets using the SGSGID
If no, ENR will extract the TERM DATE from Facets using the Member CK.
In either case, if there are no records found then ENR will set the TERM DATE to “12/31/2199”.

ENR will check if FACETS TERM DATE is not “12/31/2199” and intake Eligibility Term Date > Facets Term Date.
ENR will check if the validation “TermDateMisMatchIgnoreNewSpan” is configured in the configuration table and Intake Transaction Type is ‘Change’ and Facets Effective Date is not ‘null’ and Facets Effective Date!= Intake Eligibility Date then ENR will not throw any validation Error.
If the above condition is not true, then ENR should set the error type as “Warning” and an event should be logged in ENR with the following message “Eligibility Term Date in inbound 834 File is greater than the termination Date in Facets”

11.3. Cancellation Supplemental Instructions (Member Level) 

A cancellation transaction is initiated when the enrollment is to be ended without coverage ever being 

effectuated. A cancellation can occur any time prior to, on or after, the effective date of initial coverage. A 

cancellation is defined by the enrollment end date being equal to the enrollment start date. 

This transaction is used when the Exchange cancels individuals in the enrollment group rather than the 

entire enrollment group. This will only be used by the Exchange to communicate member level cancellations 

to Issuers. Issuers will not use this transaction to send cancellations to the Exchange. 

All members of an enrollment group are included in maintenance 834 transactions except for cancel/term of 

the subscriber, when only the subscriber loop is sent. 

Additional maintenance reason codes that have suffix qualifiers (e.g., “CANCEL-NLE,” “TERM-OTH”) are not 

supported by the Exchange. 

Note: CMS does not use a member level cancellation transaction.

{"id":640764,"title":"(ENR SUCC) DEV & TEST - 834E/U AR PASSE Transaction Effective Date Logic Update - EDI","description":"<p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><strong></strong> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;font-weight:400;\"> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><strong>Overview</strong> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">This feature details the functionality required to correct the improper entry of split spans in Facets, based on Eligibility Date and Assessment Date, for changes received via EDI 834 E and U. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Business Rules &amp; Requirements </h3><ol style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date 2000 Loop (DTP*356/DTP*348) from the EDI 834 as the transaction effective date for all new enrollments, regardless of the Assessment Date. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date = 1/24/25, use Eligibility Date (1/31/25). </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility, if the Assessment Date has changed. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date changes to 6/29/25, use Assessment Date (6/29/25). </li><li>The business needs to update the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility when the Assessment Date changes, but none of the other elements listed below have changed:<ul><li>Assessment Number </li><li>Assessment Tier </li><li>Assessment Division </li><li>Aid Category </li><li>Rate Cell </li><li>Pregnancy </li> </ul> </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received prior to the Eligibility Date. </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Maintenance Date (DTP*303) as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received after the Eligibility Date. </li> </ol><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Current State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">Currently, Maintenance effective date is being used to split spans on Update files. This is causing mismatches with capitation calculations, and the Finance team is misreporting revenue. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">What is Changing </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date 2000 Loop (DTP*303) cannot be used for all change transactions. Depending on the change, and whether it is received prior to or after the initial Eligibility Date, the transaction effective date may reflect either the Assessment Date, Eligibility Date, or Maintenance Date. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Future State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date will no longer be used to split spans based on Update (834) files, except as detailed in Requirement 4 above. The transaction dates in Facets will conform to the functionality detailed in Requirements 1-5. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Assumptions </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">None identified. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Dependencies/Considerations </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">None identified. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Risks </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date = 1/24/25, use Eligibility Date (1/31/25). </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility, if the Assessment Date has changed. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date changes to 6/29/25, use Assessment Date (6/29/25). </li><li>The business needs to update the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility when the Assessment Date changes, but none of the other elements listed below have changed:<ul><li>Assessment Number </li><li>Assessment Tier </li><li>Assessment Division </li><li>Aid Category </li><li>Rate Cell </li><li>Pregnancy </li> </ul> </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received prior to the Eligibility Date. </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Maintenance Date (DTP*303) as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received after the Eligibility Date. </li> </ol><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Current State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">Currently, Maintenance effective date is being used to split spans on Update files. # Agent 2 — Test Scenario Generation (User Story → Test Scenarios)




## ROLE




You are a test scenario generation agent for EDI 834 inbound files. You receive user story details from the previous agent (Agent 1) and generate only test scenarios (not test cases) derived strictly from the combination of the description and acceptance criteria of that user story.




## INPUT




- User story details are passed in from the previous agent (Agent 1). Do NOT call Azure DevOps directly. Use the user story content, description, and acceptance criteria provided to you by Agent 1.




- This includes, word for word and without summarization:




  - The full Description — every line, every bullet, every section




  - The full Acceptance Criteria — every AC scenario, every Given/When/Then line, the full Definition of Ready (DoR), and the full Definition of Done (DoD)




## INSTRUCTIONS




1. Consume the user story details received from the previous agent (Agent 1), including title, description, acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then), Definition of Ready, and Definition of Done for EDI 834 inbound files.




2. Parse and semantically analyze both the description and the acceptance criteria together — including every Given/When/Then line, DoR, and DoD — to extract functional and non-functional requirements. Generate test scenarios that are very specific to the description and acceptance criteria combined, as provided by Agent 1 [MUST]. The description often carries contextual/business intent that must be used alongside the acceptance criteria to shape each scenario — acceptance criteria alone MUST NOT be treated as the sole source.




3. Treat DoR as the precondition/setup context (what must be true before the scenario can be executed) and DoD as the completion/exit criteria (what confirms the scenario is fully satisfied). Use both to shape preconditions and expected outcomes at the scenario level — do NOT ignore or drop DoR/DoD content when generating scenarios [MUST].




4. Reference the provided EDI 834 knowledge base and historical manual test scenarios to understand how the scenarios should be framed and all the different situations that need to be covered. Generate test scenarios that are specific to EDI 834 inbound and refer the process steps in the knowledge base STRICTLY [MUST].




5. Generate comprehensive and specific test scenarios covering positive, negative, and edge conditions, ensuring all possible situations are included, and generate them based on the description and acceptance criteria combination (including Given/When/Then, DoR, DoD) specific to inbound [MUST].




6. Produce only test scenarios — a concise, one-line statement of what is to be validated for each acceptance criterion, informed by the corresponding description context. Do NOT generate detailed test steps, expected results, or full test cases (that is Agent 3's responsibility).




7. For each test scenario, populate the fields: `scenarioId`, `title`, `descriptionRef`, `acceptanceCriteriaRef` (Given/When/Then text), `dorRef`, `dodRef`, `type` (Positive / Negative / Edge), `description`, and `priority`.




8. Validate each scenario against formatting and content rules; if any validation fails, regenerate the scenario until full compliance is achieved.




9. Provide error handling for missing data, incomplete stories, or knowledge base gaps with fallback strategies (e.g., flag the gap in the scenario `description` and continue with the remaining criteria). If the description, DoR, or DoD is missing or empty, fall back to acceptance-criteria-only generation and flag this in the `description` field.




STRICT RULES:




- NEVER replace the description, acceptance criteria, Given/When/Then lines, DoR, or DoD with a summary line.




- NEVER paraphrase, consolidate, shorten, or omit any part of them.




- Do NOT hallucinate — every scenario must be traceable to the description, AC (Given/When/Then), DoR, DoD, or KB provided.




## SCENARIO VOLUME DISCIPLINE [MUST]




- Produce a MAXIMUM of 4 test scenarios per user story. This is a hard limit.




- When the user story contains more than 4 candidate scenarios, select the 4 that carry the highest business risk and the widest coverage of the acceptance criteria, and set `priority` accordingly (High first). Merge closely related acceptance criteria into a single scenario rather than dropping coverage silently.




- Every scenario you emit MUST be materially different from the others. Do NOT emit near-duplicate scenarios that validate the same mechanism with different wording.




- This limit exists because the downstream test case generator expands every scenario into 3 test cases of 15-20 steps each, and the platform enforces a 600-second execution ceiling on the workflow. Exceeding 4 scenarios causes the downstream run to time out and produce nothing.




## OUTPUT FORMAT




- JSON array of test scenario objects. Each object must contain:




  - `scenarioId` — unique identifier (e.g., `TS_001`)




  - `title` — short scenario name




  - `descriptionRef` — the relevant excerpt from the user story description that informs this scenario




  - `acceptanceCriteriaRef` — the acceptance criterion (full Given/When/Then text) this scenario maps to




  - `dorRef` — the relevant Definition of Ready item(s), if any, that this scenario depends on. Use an empty string if the user story has no Definition of Ready — do NOT invent one.




  - `dodRef` — the relevant Definition of Done item(s), if any, that confirm this scenario's completion. Use an empty string if the user story has no Definition of Done — do NOT invent one.




  - `type` — `Positive` | `Negative` | `Edge`




  - `description` — one-line statement of what is validated, reflecting the description, AC, DoR, and DoD context




  - `priority` — `High` | `Medium` | `Low`




- Data must be clean, validated, and ready to be consumed by the next agent (Agent 3).




- Emit the JSON array and nothing else. No prose before or after it.




## SAMPLE




```json




[




  {




    "scenarioId": "TS_001",




    "title": "Valid 834 inbound File Generation",




    "descriptionRef": "The system must process enrollment data submitted by trading partners and generate a valid EDI 834 inbound file for downstream consumption.",




    "acceptanceCriteriaRef": "AC1 - Given valid enrollment data is submitted, When the 834 inbound file is generated, Then the system produces a valid EDI 834 file with correct segments",




    "dorRef": "DoR - Trading partner enrollment test data available in staging environment",




    "dodRef": "DoD - Generated file passes segment validation and is archived successfully",




    "type": "Positive",




    "description": "Validate that the system generates a valid EDI 834 inbound file with correct segments when valid enrollment data is provided, consistent with the described enrollment processing flow.",




    "priority": "High"




  },




  {




    "scenarioId": "TS_002",




    "title": "834 Generation with Missing Subscriber Data",




    "descriptionRef": "The system must validate mandatory subscriber fields before generating the 834 file, as outlined in the story description.",




    "acceptanceCriteriaRef": "AC2 - Given mandatory subscriber data is missing, When the 834 inbound file is generated, Then the system rejects or flags the file",




    "dorRef": "DoR - Test file with intentionally missing mandatory subscriber fields prepared",




    "dodRef": "DoD - Rejection/error is logged and visible in Transaction Management UI",




    "type": "Negative",




    "description": "Validate that the system rejects or flags the 834 inbound file generation when mandatory subscriber data is missing, per the validation behavior described in the story.",




    "priority": "High"




  },




  {




    "scenarioId": "TS_003",




    "title": "834 Generation at Maximum Member Volume",




    "descriptionRef": "The story description notes the system must scale to support high-volume enrollment batches without failure.",




    "acceptanceCriteriaRef": "AC3 - Given the maximum supported member volume, When a single 834 inbound file is generated, Then the system processes it without failure",




    "dorRef": "DoR - Maximum-volume mock file prepared per trading partner spec",




    "dodRef": "DoD - File processed successfully within expected processing time with no data loss",




    "type": "Edge",




    "description": "Validate that the system correctly generates the 834 inbound file at the maximum supported member volume boundary described in the story.",




    "priority": "Medium"




  }




]




```

For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date = 1/24/25, use Eligibility Date (1/31/25). </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility, if the Assessment Date has changed. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date changes to 6/29/25, use Assessment Date (6/29/25). </li><li>The business needs to update the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility when the Assessment Date changes, but none of the other elements listed below have changed:<ul><li>Assessment Number </li><li>Assessment Tier </li><li>Assessment Division </li><li>Aid Category </li><li>Rate Cell </li><li>Pregnancy </li> </ul> </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received prior to the Eligibility Date. </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Maintenance Date (DTP*303) as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received after the Eligibility Date. </li> </ol><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Current State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">Currently, Maintenance effective date is being used to split spans on Update files. This is causing mismatches with capitation calculations, and the Finance team is misreporting revenue. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">What is Changing </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date 2000 Loop (DTP*303) cannot be used for all change transactions. 3.16. Member Matching Logic
The business rules for Member Matching Logic are as follows. 

3.16.1. Medicaid ID
· SearchMember based on the MEDICAID ID (Loop 2000->REF*0F). The output of SearchMember would provide the MEME_CK within the same group.
· If the MEME_CK is found, then the member is present based on the Medicaid ID.
3.16.2. Prior Medicaid Id 
If the member is not found using the Medicaid Id, then check to see if the member exists in the MEST using he prior Medicaid ID (REF*Q4)
3.16.3. Date of Birth, SSN and Name
· ENR should check if the member is present in Facets based on DOB, SSN, First Name and Last Name using the FXI API. If MEME_CK is found, then the member is present in Facets.
· If the SSN is not 9-digit valid numeric value (for e.g. 9999999999, 000000000) then do no use the SSN for match by demographics. Just use first name, last name and DOB. 
· If there are multiple MEME_CK found, then ENR should error out the transa

· If Loop 2000/2100G/NM1 Segment (Responsible Person) is present then ENR should set the Member Type value in the ECF as “4”.
· If Loop 2000/2100H/NM1 Segment (Drop Off Location) is present then ENR should set the Member Type value in the ECF as “5”.
· ENR should be configured to read these codes from a configuration File.

ts to Edifecs Enrollment Management solution’s features and functions, classification of requirements into categories identifying different degrees of feature match and overview the implementation assumptions. This document will cover the implementation of the Edifecs ENR Solution & Approach.
The document provides high level information about how the out-of-box Edifecs Enrollment Management solution can be implemented along with comparisons to Edifecs product based on requirements. It shall also provide insight with regard to how CareSource would like the solution to be configured to meet business requirements. The Technical details of this implementation are out of scope for this document and instead shall be covered by a separate Technical Design document.
1.1. Definitions
The below terms have been used to define certain aspects of the Edifecs solution and the work effort involved for the relative requirement:
· Out of box – This term clarifies that the requirement associated with this work effort is a pre-defined functionality which is implemented as part of the ENR Product 8.11 and does not require any customization.
· Configuration – This term is used to specify that the associated requirement is not out of the box and will involve some effort on the implementation of consultants’ part to configure.
· Customization –This term has been used to denote that the associated requirement is a complex code and will take significant effort (custom code) to implement.

· Not Supported – With current product offering and in given timelines, the requested requirement cannot be supported by customization or Custom development.

2. Solution Overview

2.1. Business Problem and Solution
Edifecs ENR will bring in industry standard EDI compliance validation and acknowledgement generation best practices. Edifecs ENR will also bring file tracking, alerting mechanisms as well as intuitive user interface for EDI data management. Edifecs ENR provides drools-based rules framework that will be utilized to implement large amounts of current Facets validations in Edifecs layer. These validations put erroneous transactions into the Edifecs ENR workflow for manual review and intervention, thus ensuring only cleaned and validated enrollment data goes downstream to existing enrollment services layer. 
2.2. Products Involved

	Product
	Version/Specifics
	Purpose

	Edifecs Smart Trading (ST)
	TM 9.0.0.x
	This is underlying platform solution for Edifecs ENR solution and details of its configuration are beyond scope of this document (and will be outlined in separate Fit Gap Analysis document to cover other non-enrollment transactions like 270-271, 276-277 etc.)

	
Edifecs Enrollment Management (ENR)
	
ENR 8.11.x
	The Edifecs Enrollment Management solution serves as a pre-processing enrollment solution in managing the workflow between the various intake systems and the membership system while ensuring enrollment record accuracy between the two systems.




2.3. Assumptions
· Edifecs will use ENR v8.11.x for implementation (ENR along with underlying Smart Trading solution may receive one or more patches during implementation). 
· ENR Solution will be deployed on servers hosted by CareSource.
· CareSource enrollment business operations users will work errored transactions via workflow in Edifecs ENR solution and ensure timely actions on enrollment traffic that need manual review.
· If State Medicaid sends more than 1 daily changes-only files to Edifecs ENR, Edifecs Implementation team may configure via either of the two options
· One account with multiple trade relationships
· Multiple accounts, each with 1 trade relationship
· Edifecs will use the Companion Guide version date August 19, 2024, for this implementation. Link to the companion guide: https://www.medicaid.nv.gov/providers/edi 
· One daily change only file and one monthly audit file is expected for this implementation.
· ENR should Use 356 and 348 for effective dates and use DTP*357 and DTP*349 for termination. 
· Edifecs will reuse the existing solution implemented for other Medicaid LOBs and modify it as per the NV specific requirements documented in this Fitgap.
· The change file should only update the demographics and not change the eligibility. 
· Change file should not create a new member transaction. Send the transaction to EWL if the member in the change file is a non-existing Facets member. 
· For Retro terms we expect to see a term date along with a matching effective date in the Facets that the state wants us to update in 021 and 030. 
· For retro changes, it is assumed that the state will send a void first and then send a retro add in a separate transaction. Retro is expected to come in 021 and 030 only and not in 001 transaction type
· 001 transaction type should not create a new member. 
· 001 should not change the SBEL, but update the SBSG, MECD, MECM, MEIA, MEHD (TBD), MELC (TBD) if the aid category changes or subgroup changes. 
· 001 should only be used for demo

1. Introduction
The purpose of this Fit Gap and scope document is to provide clarity to both CareSource and Edifecs teams on various business requirements for implementation of Edifecs Enrollment Management (“ENR”) solution. This includes but is not limited to: Mapping of CareSource’s requirements to Edifecs Enrollment Management solution’s features and functions, classification of requirements into categories identifying different degrees of feature match and also overview the implementation assumptions. This document will cover implementation of the Edifecs ENR Solution & Approach.
The document provides high level information about how the out of box Edifecs Enrollment Management solution can be implemented along with comparisons to Edifecs product based on particular requirements. It shall also provide insight in with regards to how CareSource would like the solution to be configured to meet business requirements. The Technical details of this implementation are out of scope for this document and instead shall be covered by a separate Technical Design document.
1.1. Definitions
The below terms have been used to define certain aspects of the Edifecs solution and the work effort involved for the relative requirement:
· Out of box – This term clarifies that the requirement associated with this work effort is a pre-defined functionality which is implemented as part of the ENR Product 8.11 and does not require any customization.
· Configuration – This term is used to specify that the associated requirement is not out of the box and will involve some effort on the implementation consultants’ part to configure.
· Customization –This term has been used to denote that the associated requirement is a complex code and will take significant effort (custom code) to implement.

· Not Supported – With current product offering and in given timelines, the requested requirement cannot be supported by customization or Custom development.

2. Solution Overview

1.1. Business Problem and Solution
CareSource currently utilizes multiple homegrown systems and solutions together to process Ohio State Medicaid enrollment files. CareSource EDI Team picks up the x12 834 files and push these to preprocessor where business validations are performed. Once the records are identified as good then it is splits into ~14 flat files. Facets is updated via batch process using MMS keyword file processing. There also exists a custom-built reconciliation tool that compares intake enrollment data against data posted to Facets at end of the day and provides list of errors to enrollment recon specialists to work through.
Edifecs ENR will bring in industry standard EDI compliance validation and acknowledgement generation best practices. Edifecs ENR will also bring file sequencing, tracking, alerting mechanisms as well as intuitive user interface for EDI data management. Edifecs ENR provides drools-based rules framework that will be utilized to implement large amount of current Facets validations in Edifecs layer. These validations put erroneous transactions into Edifecs ENR workflow for manual review and intervention, thus ensuring only cleaned and validated enrollment data goes downstream to existing enrollment services layer.

    "scenarioId": "TS_001",
    "title": "Populate Eligibility Date as transaction effective date for inbound 834 when eligibility span has not yet begun",
    "descriptionRef": "This feature details the functionality required to correct the improper entry of split spans in Facets, based on Eligibility Date and Assessment Date, for changes received via EDI 834 E and U. \nThe business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date 2000 Loop (DTP*356/DTP*348) from the EDI 834 as the transaction effective date for all new enrollments, regardless of the Assessment Date. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date = 1/24/25, use Eligibility Date (1/31/25). \nCurrent State \nCurrently, Maintenance effective date is being used to split spans on Update files. This is causing mismatches with capitation calculations, and the Finance team is misreporting revenue. \nWhat is Changing \nThe Maintenance Date 2000 Loop (DTP*303) cannot be used for all change transactions. Depending on the change, and whether it is received prior to or after the initial Eligibility Date, the transaction effective date may reflect either the Assessment Date, Eligibility Date, or Maintenance Date. \nFuture State \nThe Maintenance Date will no longer be used to split spans based on Update (834) files, except as detailed in Requirement 4 above. The transaction dates in Facets will conform to the functionality detailed in Requirements 1-5. \nExamples / Scenarios \nScenario | Eligibility Started? | Transaction Effective Date \nNew enrollment (Future eligibility date) | No | Eligibility Date \nTechnical Notes \nData values are contained in the 834 transaction loops as follows: \nAssessment Date - Loop 2300, HD03 \nEffective Date - Loop 2000, DTP03 \nMaintenance Date - Loop 2000, DTP01 \nAdjust logic to selectively use Eligibility Date, Assessment Date, or Maintenance Date as transaction effective date based on the outlined business rules. \nEnsure backward compatibility with existing EDI processing where applicable. \nWhen multiple dates come in, use the first one.",
    "acceptanceCriteriaRef": "3. Given an inbound EDI 834 file, if the member’s eligibility span has not yet begun, the Eligibility Date (DTP*356/DTP*348) populates as the transaction effective date.",

    "dodRef": "1. All functionality detailed in the feature has been developed, implemented, and tested in Production. \n2. - One row per test case should be considered; Test Step # / Test Step Description / Test Step Expected Result / Test Step Attachment should be sub-rows within that single test case row. Do not produce repetitive test cases in output — all test case details should be in the first line except test step sub-rows [STRICTLY].
- **Id Column** must start as `TC_001`, `TC_002`, and so on. It should NOT start with ADO US or any number — only provide ADO details for specific test cases where applicable.
- Data must be clean, validated, and ready for import into test management systems.
**Description:**  
## INPUT




- **Test scenario (JSON) — REQUIRED, variable `scenariojson`:** A JSON array of test scenarios from the previous agent (Agent 2). Each scenario contains `scenarioId`, `title`, `descriptionRef`, `acceptanceCriteriaRef`, `dorRef`, `dodRef`, `type`, `description`, and `priority`. Use these scenarios — including the description context and DoR/DoD references — as the basis for test case generation. Do NOT call Azure DevOps directly.




- **reworknotes — OPTIONAL, variable `reworknotes`:** Free-text/JSON feedback produced by the downstream LLM-as-a-Judge reviewer in a previous round (may include `feedback`, `gaps`, and `strengths`). When this variable is present and non-empty, treat it as the HIGHEST-PRIORITY instruction set for this round and follow the "FEEDBACK HANDLING" section below. When it is empty/blank, this is the first round — generate normally.

## FEEDBACK HANDLING (applies ONLY when `reworknotes` is present and non-empty)




When the reworknotes contains content from a previous round, this is a REGENERATION round. You MUST:




1. **Parse the feedback into a checklist.** Extract every distinct point from the `feedback`, `gaps`, and `strengths` fields. Treat each `gap` and each `feedback` sentence as a mandatory action item you have to resolve THIS round.




2. **Refine, do NOT regenerate from scratch.** Start from the intent of the previous round's test cases and IMPROVE them to resolve the feedback. Do NOT balloon the output — keep the total number of test cases within the limits in "OUTPUT VOLUME DISCIPLINE". Do NOT emit duplicate or near-duplicate test cases.




3. **Explicitly resolve each recurring item.** The reviewer repeatedly asks for the following — you MUST satisfy ALL of them in every regeneration round:




   - **Traceability:** every test case MUST populate the `ScenarioId` and `AcceptanceCriteriaRef` columns, tying it to exactly one input scenario/AC.




   - **Atomicity:** every test case MUST validate exactly ONE mechanism/behavior. If a case bundles multiple independent validations, SPLIT it into separate dedicated test cases.




   - **Scenario-specific preconditions:** the `Precondition` MUST reference the exact data, file, state/LOB, and system state required by that scenario — never a generic phrase like "User story implemented".




   - **Concrete, measurable expected results:** every expected result MUST be specific and verifiable (exact status value, exact SQL table/row condition, exact archive path, exact segment/value) — never vague wording like "works correctly" or "as expected".




   - **Type balance:** ensure a sensible balance of Positive, Negative, and Edge cases per acceptance criterion.




4. **Verify every item is resolved before you output.** Walk your checklist from step 1 and confirm each feedback point and each gap has been concretely addressed in the regenerated test cases. Do NOT add a changelog, a `## Changes Made This Round` section, or any other narrative to your output. The output object must contain exactly the two fields `testcases` and `scenariojson` and nothing else — any extra text before, after, or between them breaks the downstream reviewer, which parses your output as JSON [MUST].




## INSTRUCTIONS




1. Consume the scenariojson received as input, each mapped to a description + acceptance criteria combination (with `dorRef`/`dodRef`) for EDI 834 Inbound files. If `reworknotes` is non-empty, first apply the FEEDBACK HANDLING section above, then proceed.




2. Parse and semantically analyze each test scenario — including its `descriptionRef`, `acceptanceCriteriaRef`, `dorRef`, and `dodRef` — to extract functional and non-functional requirements. Generate test cases very specific to the test scenario and its referenced description, acceptance criteria, DoR, and DoD received from Agent 2 [MUST]. Do NOT treat `acceptanceCriteriaRef` alone as sufficient — the `descriptionRef` context must directly shape the test case's steps and expected results.




3. Reference the provided EDI 834 knowledge base and historical manual test cases to understand how test cases should be generated and all the different scenarios that need to be covered. Generate test cases specific to EDI 834 Inbound. Follow the process steps in the knowledge base STRICTLY, and generate detailed test step descriptions step by step that reference the relevant documents like the output sample template in the knowledge base [MUST].




4. STRICTLY: Refer `kb_edi_834_testcase_analysis_1_embedded` to cover both the database details and the server name details [MUST]. When referencing any knowledge base file, you MUST open it, read it thoroughly, and extract the actual concrete details from it — real server name, database name, database engine, table names, column names, and queries — and embed those literal values directly into the test step description. Do NOT merely cite or name the KB file. Never leave a KB name unresolved in a test step [MUST].




4a. **Schema-grounded SQL [MUST]:** For every test step that includes a database validation query, you MUST fetch and open the schema knowledge base `kb_edi_schema_details_003_large` (the authoritative source of Facets/staging schema details — full database schema including table names, column names, primary/foreign keys, datatypes, and table relationships), read it thoroughly, and build each SQL query from the actual, literal object names defined in it. This knowledge base contains three schema documents, each with a distinct role:




   - `EDI and FACETS Schema 2` — the authoritative source for the FACETS database tables, including the member/subscriber/eligibility tables and their exact table names, column names, keys, datatypes, and relationships. All FACETS member-data verification steps MUST resolve their table and column names from this document.




   - `Facets 834` — the source for the 834-to-FACETS mapping details (how inbound 834 segments/elements map to FACETS fields and staging structures).




   - `EDIFECS Full with AUX 834` — the source for the full Edifecs 834 layout including AUX segments/elements used during processing and validation.




   All tables (e.g., the crosswalk, MELC, the FACETS member/subscriber/eligibility tables, and any others), columns, joins, and filter predicates used in a query MUST match the exact names, datatypes, and key relationships defined in the applicable document above — never invent, guess, hardcode, or approximate table/column names. Resolve the schema details into concrete, executable SQL embedded directly in the Test Step Description; never leave a document name or any schema element from it as an unresolved placeholder or citation in a test step [MUST]. Where `kb_edi_834_testcase_analysis_1_embedded` (server/database) and `kb_edi_schema_details_003_large` (schema/table/column definitions) overlap, cross-reference both so the query targets the correct server and database with the correct, schema-accurate object names.




5. Use `dorRef` to derive each test case's Precondition field — the setup/data/environment state that must exist before execution — and use `dodRef` to derive the final expected outcome / last test step's Expected Result — confirming what "done" looks like for that scenario [MUST]. Never drop or ignore `dorRef`/`dodRef` content when populating these fields, even though these references are not output as separate columns.




5a. **No meta-referencing of source fields [MUST]:** The output must never explicitly name, cite, or refer to `dorRef`, `dodRef`, `descriptionRef`, "DoR", "DoD", "Definition of Ready", "Definition of Done", "per the AC", "as referenced in", or any similar meta-label anywhere in the Name, Description, Precondition, Test Step Description, or Test Step Expected Result fields. This also applies to knowledge base sources: never name `kb_edi_834_testcase_analysis_1_embedded`, `kb_edi_schema_details_003_large`, `EDI and FACETS Schema 2`, or any KB file in the output text — only their resolved, concrete values (server names, database names, table/column names, queries) may appear. The content derived from these sources must appear as plain, self-contained precondition/setup statements and plain, self-contained outcome statements — written as if they are simply facts about the test, not as citations of where they came from.

6. 6a. **Related acceptance criteria consolidation:** Before generating test cases, evaluate whether two (or more) acceptance criteria — including their `descriptionRef`, `dorRef`, and `dodRef` context — are functionally related or interdependent. 6b. **Multi-state coverage [MUST]:** A single user story may involve one, several, or all states/LOBs. Before generating test cases, you MUST enumerate every state/LOB referenced anywhere in the scenario's `descriptionRef`, `acceptanceCriteriaRef`, `dorRef`, and `dodRef` (as well as the user story title and description) and build the complete list of applicable states for that user story. Do NOT hardcode, assume, or limit to a single state (e.g., do not default to `MI` or `AR`). The applicable states are whatever the user story context actually specifies — this may be a specific subset, or "all states" if the story is state-agnostic or explicitly applies to every state.




   - **PREFER PARAMETERIZATION.** When the behaviour under test is identical across states, write ONE test case and parameterize the state so the same case is explicitly executable for every applicable state, naming the full applicable-state set in the Precondition. Only generate a separate test case per state when the expected behaviour genuinely differs between states. Duplicating every case per state multiplies the output and will breach the volume limits below.




   - If the user story applies to all states, treat "all states" as the coverage set and generate state-agnostic test cases whose steps are written to be valid for any state, while still resolving concrete state/trading-partner values in each executed instance.




   - If the user story names a single state, generate for that state only.




   - Never omit a state that is present in the description, acceptance criteria, DoR, or DoD. Every applicable state must be covered and reflected in the resolved file names, staging/archive paths, and trading-partner filters within the test steps.




Generate the test cases in a structured format — do not combine all steps in a single row. Place each individual test step in its own row under the "Test Step Description" column and provide the corresponding "Test Step Expected Result" in that same row for that specific step; every test step must have its own expected result [MUST].

For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date = 1/24/25, use Eligibility Date (1/31/25). </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility, if the Assessment Date has changed. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date changes to 6/29/25, use Assessment Date (6/29/25). </li><li>The business needs to update the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility when the Assessment Date changes, but none of the other elements listed below have changed:<ul><li>Assessment Number </li><li>Assessment Tier </li><li>Assessment Division </li><li>Aid Category </li><li>Rate Cell </li><li>Pregnancy </li> </ul> </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received prior to the Eligibility Date. </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Maintenance Date (DTP*303) as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received after the Eligibility Date. </li> </ol><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Current State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">Currently, Maintenance effective date is being used to split spans on Update files. This is causing mismatches with capitation calculations, and the Finance team is misreporting revenue. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">What is Changing </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date 2000 Loop (DTP*303) cannot be used for all change transactions. {"id":640764,"title":"(ENR SUCC) DEV & TEST - 834E/U AR PASSE Transaction Effective Date Logic Update - EDI","description":"<p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><strong></strong> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;font-weight:400;\"> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><strong>Overview</strong> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">This feature details the functionality required to correct the improper entry of split spans in Facets, based on Eligibility Date and Assessment Date, for changes received via EDI 834 E and U. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Business Rules &amp; Requirements </h3><ol style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date 2000 Loop (DTP*356/DTP*348) from the EDI 834 as the transaction effective date for all new enrollments, regardless of the Assessment Date. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date = 1/24/25, use Eligibility Date (1/31/25). </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility, if the Assessment Date has changed. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date changes to 6/29/25, use Assessment Date (6/29/25). </li><li>The business needs to update the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility when the Assessment Date changes, but none of the other elements listed below have changed:<ul><li>Assessment Number </li><li>Assessment Tier </li><li>Assessment Division </li><li>Aid Category </li><li>Rate Cell </li><li>Pregnancy </li> </ul> </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received prior to the Eligibility Date. </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Maintenance Date (DTP*303) as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received after the Eligibility Date. </li> </ol><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Current State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">Currently, Maintenance effective date is being used to split spans on Update files. This is causing mismatches with capitation calculations, and the Finance team is misreporting revenue. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">What is Changing </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date 2000 Loop (DTP*303) cannot be used for all change transactions. Depending on the change, and whether it is received prior to or after the initial Eligibility Date, the transaction effective date may reflect either the Assessment Date, Eligibility Date, or Maintenance Date. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Future State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date will no longer be used to split spans based on Update (834) files, except as detailed in Requirement 4 above. The transaction dates in Facets will conform to the functionality detailed in Requirements 1-5. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Assumptions </h3><p {"id":640764,"title":"(ENR SUCC) DEV & TEST - 834E/U AR PASSE Transaction Effective Date Logic Update - EDI","description":"<p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><strong></strong> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;font-weight:400;\"> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><strong>Overview</strong> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">This feature details the functionality required to correct the improper entry of split spans in Facets, based on Eligibility Date and Assessment Date, for changes received via EDI 834 E and U. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Business Rules &amp; Requirements </h3><ol style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date 2000 Loop (DTP*356/DTP*348) from the EDI 834 as the transaction effective date for all new enrollments, regardless of the Assessment Date. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date = 1/24/25, use Eligibility Date (1/31/25). </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility, if the Assessment Date has changed. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date changes to 6/29/25, use Assessment Date (6/29/25). </li><li>The business needs to update the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility when the Assessment Date changes, but none of the other elements listed below have changed:<ul><li>Assessment Number </li><li>Assessment Tier </li><li>Assessment Division </li><li>Aid Category </li><li>Rate Cell </li><li>Pregnancy </li> </ul> </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received prior to the Eligibility Date. </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Maintenance Date (DTP*303) as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received after the Eligibility Date. </li> </ol><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Current State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">Currently, Maintenance effective date is being used to split spans on Update files. This is causing mismatches with capitation calculations, and the Finance team is misreporting revenue. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">What is Changing </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date 2000 Loop (DTP*303) cannot be used for all change transactions. Depending on the change, and whether it is received prior to or after the initial Eligibility Date, the transaction effective date may reflect either the Assessment Date, Eligibility Date, or Maintenance Date. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Future State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date will no longer be used to split spans based on Update (834) files, except as detailed in Requirement 4 above. The transaction dates in Facets will conform to the functionality detailed in Requirements 1-5. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Assumptions </h3><p {"id":640764,"title":"(ENR SUCC) DEV & TEST - 834E/U AR PASSE Transaction Effective Date Logic Update - EDI","description":"<p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><strong></strong> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;font-weight:400;\"> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><strong>Overview</strong> </p><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">This feature details the functionality required to correct the improper entry of split spans in Facets, based on Eligibility Date and Assessment Date, for changes received via EDI 834 E and U. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Business Rules &amp; Requirements </h3><ol style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\"><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date 2000 Loop (DTP*356/DTP*348) from the EDI 834 as the transaction effective date for all new enrollments, regardless of the Assessment Date. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date = 1/24/25, use Eligibility Date (1/31/25). </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility, if the Assessment Date has changed. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date changes to 6/29/25, use Assessment Date (6/29/25). </li><li>The business needs to update the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility when the Assessment Date changes, but none of the other elements listed below have changed:<ul><li>Assessment Number </li><li>Assessment Tier </li><li>Assessment Division </li><li>Aid Category </li><li>Rate Cell </li><li>Pregnancy </li> </ul> </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received prior to the Eligibility Date. </li><li>The business needs to utilize the Maintenance Date (DTP*303) as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received after the Eligibility Date. </li> </ol><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Current State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">Currently, Maintenance effective date is being used to split spans on Update files. This is causing mismatches with capitation calculations, and the Finance team is misreporting revenue. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">What is Changing </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date 2000 Loop (DTP*303) cannot be used for all change transactions. Depending on the change, and whether it is received prior to or after the initial Eligibility Date, the transaction effective date may reflect either the Assessment Date, Eligibility Date, or Maintenance Date. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Future State </h3><p style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:medium;\">The Maintenance Date will no longer be used to split spans based on Update (834) files, except as detailed in Requirement 4 above. The transaction dates in Facets will conform to the functionality detailed in Requirements 1-5. </p><h3 style=\"font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;\">Assumptions </h3><p the transaction effective date for all new enrollments, regardless of the Assessment Date. This is causing mismatches with capitation calculations, and the Finance team is misreporting revenue. \nWhat is Changing \nThe Maintenance Date 2000 Loop (DTP*303) cannot be used for all change transactions. Facets, based on Eligibility Date and Assessment Date, for changes received via EDI 834 E and U. \nThe business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date 2000 Loop (DTP*356/DTP*348) from the EDI 834 as the transaction effective date for all new enrollments, regardless of the Assessment Date. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date = 1/24/25, use Eligibility Date (1/31/25). \nCurrent State \nCurrently, Maintenance effective date is being used to split spans on Update files. This is causing mismatches with capitation calculations, and the Finance team is misreporting revenue. \nWhat is Changing \nThe Maintenance Date 2000 Loop (DTP*303) cannot be used for all change transactions. Depending on the change, and whether it is received prior to or after the initial Eligibility Date, the transaction effective date may reflect either the Assessment Date, Eligibility Date, or Maintenance Date. \nExamples / Scenarios \nScenario | Eligibility Started? | Transaction Effective Date \nNew enrollment (Future eligibility date) | No | Eligibility Date \nTechnical Notes \nData values are contained in the 834 transaction loops as follows: \nAssessment Date - Loop 2300, HD03 \nEffective Date - Loop 2000, DTP03 \nMaintenance Date - Loop 2000, DTP01 \nAdjust logic to selectively use Eligibility Date, Assessment Date, or Maintenance Date as transaction effective date based on the outlined business rules. \nWhen multiple dates come in, use the first one.","acceptanceCriteriaRef":"1. EDI is able to identify the following dates in the EDI 834 file (existing functionality): Effective Date, Assessment Date, Maintenance Date. \n2. Given an inbound EDI 834 file, if the member’s eligibility span has not yet begun, the Eligibility Date (DTP*356/DTP*348) populates as the transaction effective date.","dorRef":"","dodRef":"1.
